reason: Re-review (retry; prior attempt delivered no verdict file) of the delivered head b96ac2976ff1c1ca59e3787dbbb302a35e18ed3f on hv/cf-mn-dead-search-cache-scan-loops-20261106 against base master e4cacdf341f83a6e2f1e135ae21262e7ec9d293a. The task body's b41287336e3bc2ccf24261ec09849e7650b50238 is a stale head reference from an earlier review round: the RETRY instruction pins the exact commit reviewed to b96ac297, which is the current local HEAD, the current origin remote SHA for the author branch (verified via git ls-remote), and the parent of the pre-existing verdict commits on this same review ref. Verified independently this attempt: (1) the diff against base is exactly the intended change -- removal of the dead 'SCAN MATCH mnemos:search:*' invalidation sweeps from mnemos/api/routes/{admin,dag,document_import}.py, mnemos/persistence/deletion_ops.py and mnemos/api/routes/acl.py (the latter two previously early-returned when _lc._cache was falsy), removal of _get_cache_key and _vis_epoch_current plus the now-unused hashlib import from mnemos/core/lifecycle.py, an unchanged-behavior comment retarget in mnemos/api/routes/memories.py, untracking of .scratch/ task artifacts that a prior refresh run had accidentally committed, and one CHANGELOG.md line under 7.1.1; (2) no live scan_iter loop or mnemos:search key construction remains anywhere in mnemos/ -- remaining grep hits are historical docstring prose only, and grep confirms zero callers of _get_cache_key / _vis_epoch_current; (3) every touched site keeps its stats-entry invalidation (stats:global / stats:global:v2, the /stats surface) and its _vis_epoch_get_incr() bump, whose consumer the MCP principal-context cache (role/namespace authorization inputs) was re-confirmed in lifecycle.py; (4) real behavioral improvement confirmed: invalidate_deletion_scope_caches and _invalidate_search_caches_after_acl_change no longer early-return on the default no-cache path (lifespan hard-wires _lc._cache to None, app.state.cache = None intact), so the visibility-epoch bump now runs on the production path; the bump stays best-effort silent on a broken epoch store; (5) tests were retargeted rather than deleted -- old SCAN-sweep pins became loud pins of the sweep's absence (fake scan_iter that pytest.fail if called, scan_calls == [] assertions) plus regression pins for helper removal, epoch-bump persistence, best-effort silence, and no bump on a 404 revoke; (6) touched suites pass at the head (tests/test_acl_routes.py + tests/test_recall_counters_parity.py: 56 passed, 1 xpassed; tests/test_deletion_request_worker.py + tests/test_persistence_parity.py: 54 passed, 1 skipped; tests/test_resilience.py: 31 passed), and a run of the remaining suite passed 1345+ before -x stopped on tests/test_doc_version_pins_match_code.py, which also fails on base master e4cacdf3 (README.md/DEPLOYMENT.md still read v7.1.0 while pyproject is 7.1.1 -- pre-existing release-doc drift, not in or near any file this branch touches); (7) the ABC-first ratchet guard (scripts/check_abc_first_guard.py) passes (the change removes code and adds no raw _lc._pool references). No correctness, security, or ABI regression found; the author branch is untouched by this review (HEAD before and after this review: b96ac2976ff1c1ca59e3787dbbb302a35e18ed3f; worktree clean) and the only write performed is this verdict artifact on the dedicated review ref. Verdict: approve.

findings.issue: The design doc still states ACL grant/revoke 'invalidate the per-user search cache (mnemos:search:*)'. That behavior was removed by this branch; only the visibility-epoch bump (and the MCP principal-context cache it drives) remains.
findings.suggestion: Update the section to describe the epoch bump. Docs-only drift, non-blocking.

findings.issue: Removals are pinned via full-module source scans (the identifier must not appear anywhere in inspect.getsource of lifecycle); a future docstring or comment mentioning either name would fail these guards spuriously.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is; optionally narrow to AST name checks if a future reference causes a false positive. Non-blocking.

findings.issue: The retained _FakeCache's scan_iter now pytest.fail if ever called (a correct loud pin), but the primed cache.store['mnemos:search:primed'] fixtures in the two tests are inert -- that key can never be deleted, so the 'not in cache.deleted' assertions are trivially satisfiable.
findings.suggestion: Optional cleanup: drop the dead mnemos:search:primed fixture lines. Non-blocking.

findings.issue: Unlike the ACL path and deletion_ops, this helper keeps its 'if not _lc._cache: return' early return, so with the runtime's None cache it skips both the stats drop and the epoch bump at its call sites (compression/restore/admin ops).
findings.suggestion: Defensible: those are not visibility-narrowing paths, and the load-bearing epoch bump (ACL grant/revoke, deletion scope) now always runs. Not a defect; noted for completeness.

verify_delivery.note: Run by the reviewer after the verdict artifact commit: baseline arg b96ac297 is the review ref's pre-verdict head (== author branch head), so the single verdict commit above it satisfies delivery.
